plan: First playable: one lab wall where tapping toggles red, green and blue spotlights and dragging them shows the mixed colors, plus 8 voiced find-this-color goals; the paint-mixing mode is left for later.

First playable: the first 20 elements as illustrated cards with voiced names and facts, placed by drag onto a simplified periodic board in 10 sorting rounds; trading, rare cards and the full table are left out.

First playable: one swaying tower scene where a tap drops the next acorn block, a center-of-mass marker shows balance and the tower collapses gently without failure, across 10 block sets; scores and leaderboards are left out.

First playable: a friendly transparent body where 8 organ pieces are dragged into big outlined slots, each answering with a voiced line and a small animation of what it does; detailed systems and quizzes are left out.
First playable: one water tank where 12 equal-size objects are dragged in to float or sink, with an optional guess-first mode over 10 rounds; changing the liquid and salt water are left for later.

First playable: a glass maze where dragging a magnet outside the glass pulls the steel bead along visible field lines through 20 authored mazes; repelling poles, timers and a level editor are left out.
First playable: 24 authored levels where tapping or swiping a rope releases a seed that swings into a planter, with pendulum trails; stars, extra gadgets and a level editor are left out.

First playable: a pull-and-release slingshot with a visible parabola preview that plants seeds in 20 authored garden plots at different heights and distances; wind and destructible structures are left out.

First playable: a workbench grid where matching atoms are dragged together to bond by valence rules, building 20 target molecules from water to glucose with voiced names; reactions and a 3D view are left out.

First playable: a breadboard grid where batteries, wires, resistors and lamps snap into place to light garden lamps in 20 authored circuits with brightness feedback; logic gates are left for a later chapter.

First playable: an optical bench where lenses and mirrors are dragged to bend light rays onto targets in 20 authored puzzles, with a focus point marker; prisms, color dispersion and free sandbox are left out.
First playable: edit and run modes for 20 chain-reaction puzzles with one missing lever, pulley, gear or ramp each, using 8 part types; free sandbox building and sharing are left out.

First playable: a free string instrument whose plucked notes draw live waves on an oscilloscope, plus 12 match-the-wave goals for pitch and loudness; microphone input and resonance experiments are left out.

First playable: one terrarium with sun and water controls where evaporation, clouds and rain play out visibly, plus 8 guided goals such as make it rain; pressure maps and a world climate view are left out.

First playable: a snap grid for beams and cables between riverbanks, a test run with a cart and tension and compression colors, over 20 authored crossings with a material limit; suspension decks and sharing are left out.

First playable: a free falling-sand canvas with 8 materials (sand, water, stone, ice, steam, lava, plant, wood) drawn by finger, plus 12 redirect-the-water goals; saving creations and a large material list are left out.

First playable: a microscope with three zoom steps and tap-to-zoom over 15 slides (cells, pond life, leaves) where moving microbes are found and added to a sticker journal; real camera input and staining are left out.

First playable: one botanical pinball table with two tap flippers, spring bumpers and momentum arrows, plus a gentle mode where the ball never drains; two extra tables and multiball are left for later.
First playable: a wide paddle bouncing a slow light sphere through 20 authored walls of research tiles, with a reflection angle guide line; power-ups, bosses and speed modes are left out.
First playable: 30 authored chamber puzzles where tapping brass pins in the right order lets water reach a seedling while sand and stones fall; hazards, timers and a level editor are left out.
